newsitem.title: USA: US CPI will be hard to cut - Labor Secretary Reich.
newsitem.headline: US CPI will be hard to cut - Labor Secretary Reich.

text.p: Labor Secretary Robert Reich said Tuesday it will be politically tough to change the Consumer Price Index for the same reasons adjusting the Medicare health plan is a hard sell.
A bipartisan Senate Commission headed by former Bush administration economist Michael Boskin has suggested adjusting the CPI by 1.1 percentage points.
Reich told a group of reporters that "neither party can unilaterally take on the CPI, nor can either party take on Medicare."
Reich called both subjects "too hot to handle because they are dealing with entitlements deemed precious by significant parts of our population."

Republicans on Capitol Hill remain angry because Democrats attacked them during the election campaign for "cutting Medicare," a charge that resonated with the seniors who benefit from it. Republicans say the attack was unfair because they were merely seeking to restrain the growth of Medicare.
The CPI is also a touchy issue because any downward adjustment would effectively limit increases in Social Security payments and other federal benefit payments that rise with inflation.
Reducing the inflation rate would also increase income taxes for more wage earners each year by lowering the minimum income threshold on top tax brackets, which rise with inflation.

"Any changes in either of these areas has to occur with a great deal of public support and understanding and has got to be justified to the public in very clear ways," Reich said of Medicare and CPI adjustments. "It's not going to be easy going."
